Build a Todo app in a single self-contained HTML file. Requirements:
- Add new todos
- Mark todos as complete (strikethrough)
- Delete todos
- Filter: All / Active / Completed
- Persist to localStorage

Deliver only the HTML file with JS, CSS, HTML. Use file name "todo_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html"

toolCallDetails.arguments:
{"path":"todo_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete, self-contained single-file Todo app HTML page with inline CSS and JS (no external dependencies). Requirements:
- Modern, clean, centered card UI with a gradient background, nice typography, rounded corners, subtle shadows.
- Header title "Todo" and an input form with a text field + "Add" button to add new todos (also submit on Enter). Trim whitespace, ignore empty input.
- Each todo item shows: a checkbox to toggle complete/incomplete (completed items get strikethrough text and reduced opacity), the todo text, and a delete button (e.g. an "x" or trash icon) that removes the item with a small fade/scale transition.
- Filter tabs/buttons: All / Active / Completed, which filter the visible list without losing data; active filter button is visually highlighted.
- A footer showing count of remaining active (not completed) todos (e.g. "3 items left") and a "Clear completed" button that removes all completed todos.
- Persist todos array (id, text, completed) to localStorage under a key like "todos-app-v1", loading them on page load, and saving after every add/toggle/delete/clear action.
- Show a friendly empty-state message when there are no todos (or none matching the current filter).
- All JS must be vanilla (no frameworks/libraries), inline in a <script> tag; all CSS inline in a <style> tag; everything in this one HTML file only.
- Use semantic HTML, accessible labels (aria-label where appropriate), and responsive layout that looks good on mobile widths too."}
